question_text: A global GenAI web app serves many users the SAME cacheable responses (e.g. generated FAQ answers and static assets) and wants to reduce latency and origin/Bedrock load worldwide. Which service caches content at edge locations near users?
explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a CDN that caches content at global edge locations, cutting latency for users and offloading repeated requests from the origin/Bedrock. Direct Connect is a dedicated on-prem link, Route 53 is DNS, and Transit Gateway interconnects VPCs/networks — none provide edge content caching.
source_topic: Amazon CloudFront edge caching for GenAI

topic: Global Accelerator for non-cacheable low latency
question_text: A real-time, streaming GenAI API has DYNAMIC, non-cacheable responses but needs improved global latency and fast regional failover by routing users over the AWS backbone to the nearest healthy endpoint. Which service fits better than a CDN here?

options.text: AWS Global Accelerator — anycast entry into the AWS backbone with fast failover for dynamic traffic
Amazon CloudFront caching with a long TTL

explanation: AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs that route users over the AWS global network to the nearest healthy regional endpoint with fast failover — ideal for dynamic, non-cacheable, latency-sensitive traffic. CloudFront caching does not help non-cacheable responses; S3 Transfer Acceleration only speeds S3 uploads; Snowball is offline transfer.
source_topic: AWS Global Accelerator for dynamic low-latency routing

question_text: A GenAI service is deployed in two Regions. The team wants DNS-level routing that automatically directs users to the lowest-latency healthy Region and fails over if one Region becomes unhealthy. Which service provides this?

options.text: Amazon Route 53 with latency-based routing and health checks/failover

explanation: Amazon Route 53 offers latency-based routing plus health checks and DNS failover to send users to the best healthy Region. WAF filters Layer-7 requests, ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, and Secrets Manager stores secrets — none provide DNS routing/failover.

question_text: An enterprise must move large volumes of on-premises documents into AWS for a Bedrock Knowledge Base over a private, consistent-bandwidth connection that avoids the public internet. Which service provides this dedicated physical connectivity?

options.text: A site-to-site connection over an internet gateway only

explanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated, private physical link between on-premises and AWS with consistent bandwidth, bypassing the public internet — suited to steady, high-volume hybrid data transfer. CloudFront is a CDN; an internet-gateway-only path traverses the public internet; Route 53 is DNS.
source_topic: AWS Direct Connect for private hybrid connectivity

question_text: A GenAI platform spans many VPCs and on-premises networks that all need to reach shared Bedrock-access and data VPCs without building a mesh of individual VPC peering connections. Which service centralizes this connectivity?

options.text: AWS Transit Gateway — a hub connecting many VPCs and on-prem networks
Individual VPC peering between every pair of VPCs

explanation: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a central hub interconnecting many VPCs and on-premises networks, replacing a complex full mesh of peering connections. Pairwise VPC peering does not scale (N-squared connections, no transitive routing); CloudFront is a CDN; Shield is DDoS protection.
source_topic: AWS Transit Gateway for multi-VPC connectivity
